explanation: The circuit of capital describes how value transforms from money capital into productive assets (machinery/labor) and commodity capital, returning as expanded money capital.

targetText: Quite apart from particular circumstances, this is necessitated by the difference, if nothing else, in the periods of production, and thus of the turnovers, of the various commodity-capitals.
explanation: Capital turnover time consists of production time plus circulation time; reducing turnover time accelerates the annual rate of profit accumulation.

targetText: These, again, are divided into fixed capital, such as machines, instruments of labour, buildings, labouring animals, etc.
explanation: Fixed capital transfers its value gradually over multiple production cycles (e.g. factory machinery), while circulating capital transfers its entire value in a single cycle (raw materials/wages).

targetText: 1) The 500v, representing wages of the labourers, and 500s, representing surplus-value of the capitalists, in department II, must be spent for articles of consumption.
explanation: Department I represents the branch of production that manufactures means of production (machinery, raw materials, industrial equipment).

targetText: 1) The 500v, representing wages of the labourers, and 500s, representing surplus-value of the capitalists, in department II, must be spent for articles of consumption.
explanation: Department II represents the branch of social production that produces consumer goods and means of individual consumption.
Social reproduction requires continuous exchange between Department I and Department II to balance industrial equipment needs with consumer wage goods.
